title.quote: An Empirical Study of Self-Admitted Technical Debt in Machine Learning Software
title.justification: The title appears at the beginning of the paper and in the ACM reference format.
title.value: An Empirical Study of Self-Admitted Technical Debt in Machine Learning Software

extractions.description: An empirical software-engineering study that mines Python projects from GitHub, detects self-admitted technical debt (SATD), compares ML and non-ML projects, manually categorizes SATD, performs survival analysis, and trains an explanatory classifier for long-lasting SATD.

type.quote: This paper aims to investigate the occurrence of SATD in ML code by analyzing 318 open-source ML projects across five domains, along with 318 non-ML projects.
type.justification: The work analyzes observed repositories, comments, commits, and SATD instances using quantitative and qualitative empirical methods.

name.quote: Software Engineering for Machine Learning (SE4ML) is a recent and rapidly evolving field
name.justification: The paper explicitly places its contribution in SE4ML and studies maintenance and lifecycle-management issues in ML software.

name.quote: Our research contributes to the understanding of technical debt in an ML context
name.justification: The central contribution concerns technical debt in ML-based software.

name.quote: Such debt is referred to as Self-Admitted Technical Debt (SATD)
name.justification: The paper advances empirical knowledge, taxonomy, and evolution analysis specifically for SATD.

name.quote: We use the Python framework PyDriller to extract all commits submitted to the repositories of our studied projects.
name.justification: Mining software repositories is used as the empirical setting and data-collection methodology rather than itself being advanced.

name.quote: Machine Learning (ML) software and traditional software
name.justification: Machine learning is the application setting in which the software-engineering claims are studied.
